scope: Characterize the LGE class system engine substrate that the d2fxxx-userdata-attribution pass named but didn't drill: the shared write helper FUN_00d272d0, member lookup FUN_00d16cd0, generic table lookup FUN_00d1df90, active-name slot writer FUN_00d11b60, the 3 small lua-state helpers (FUN_00d20490/FUN_00d204b0/FUN_00d204d0), the 5 inner-struct initializers (FUN_00d2e230 / FUN_00d2e360 / FUN_00d2e2d0 / FUN_00d1c100 / FUN_00d2efb0), and the sub-helpers FUN_00d2e4d0 / FUN_00d16080 / FUN_00d211e0.
outcome: MAJOR architectural finding: the LGE class system's underlying C++ storage type is Component::Lua::GameEngine::Work::MetamethodArray2D - Ghidra-resolved RTTI references in FUN_00d2e360 and FUN_00d2e2d0 (the two D20670 inner ctors) and in FUN_00d2e4d0 (the shared row populator) directly name this type. The BCS-Y-0509 'LGE Cursor' wrapped type is actually Component::Lua::GameEngine::Work::MetamethodArray2D::Impl (polymorphic base) with two known derived variants: ::ImplArray (allocated 0x60 bytes, no extra field) and ::ImplArray2D (allocated 0x64 bytes, extra dword at +0x18 = 2D second-dim parameter). FUN_00d211e0 is the 2D-index calculator: `width * row + col` with sentinel checks against DAT_0130d78c (invalid row) and DAT_0130d79c (invalid col). The 3 'scopes' the d2fxxx-userdata-attribution pass named (save/temp/sync) at instance struct offsets +0x60/+0x64/+0x68 are 3 ImplArray pointers - one per scope - forming the first dimension of the 2D array; member descriptors are the second dimension. FUN_00d16cd0 dispatches member lookups across the 3 scopes in priority order: own (+0x64) > save (+0x60) > sync (+0x68), tagging the active-dispatch byte at +0x30 with DAT_0130d422 (own hit) or DAT_0130d423 (sync hit) or DAT_01377fb9 (not found). FUN_00d272d0 is the 9-param polymorphic write entrypoint: vtable +0x6c on the class context, then vtable +4 on the member descriptor depending on tag byte +0xb being DAT_01377fb9 (the not-found marker - so writes to unknown members go through the default path).

modelRevision.claim: BCS-S-0041 fields +0x60/+0x64/+0x68 named save_pool/temp_pool/sync_pool wrapping D208A0 MemoryPool userdata
modelRevision.refinement: +0x60/+0x64/+0x68 hold MetamethodArray2D::Impl* pointers - each pointing to one ImplArray (or ImplArray2D) instance representing one scope's member-descriptor storage. The 'pool' interpretation is partial: each Impl IS the storage for members of one scope, but the storage isn't purely a heap allocator - it's a structured array of member descriptors keyed by name. D208A0 (BCS-Y-0506) wraps the SAME Impl objects from the Lua side, exposing _save/_temp/_sync/_reserve/_nesting/_name + the 9 size-bookkeeping fields - these are introspection accessors on the same C++ type. The model is unified: D20670 and D208A0 wrap DIFFERENT facets of the same underlying Component::Lua::GameEngine::Work::MetamethodArray2D::Impl object.
modelRevision.refinement2: The wrapped C++ type is Component::Lua::GameEngine::Work::MetamethodArray2D::Impl - the polymorphic base of the same type-family that backs the class instance's 3 scopes. So D20670 is a Lua-side view onto one of the three scope arrays directly. The 'cursor' interpretation should be replaced with 'scope view' or 'method-array row'. D20670 userdata is what scripts get when they access `instance._save` (etc) - so the wrapped object IS a scope-bucket Impl, not a cursor into anything.

phaseClosure.model: LGE class system is built on Component::Lua::GameEngine::Work::MetamethodArray2D. Each class instance has 3 ImplArray pointers (one per scope = save/own/sync). Members are stored in these arrays keyed by name. Lookups dispatch in priority order (own > save > sync). Writes go through a polymorphic dispatcher that uses the member descriptor's vtable+4. Index arithmetic for 2D variants uses width*row+col formula.
